items.title: Ray Conniff interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998
items.q: I discovered first, my first initiation into music really... was to hear the Borodin “Peasant Overture.”

ctx.x: And so it had that kind of — it was a touch of Latin beat in there too.

Yeah I think I always had that. I remember one of the early people that do interviews asked me, “what are the highlights that you think about,” you know in your whole life of music. And one of them, I mentioned that I was born in Attleboro, Massachusetts. And in our house, there was a basement. My dad practically built the house with his own hands. There was a basement, a first floor which had a kitchen, a front hall, living room and dining room, and then the second floor had the bedrooms and a bathroom, and then…

was an old Edison cylinder type Victrola. And there were some of the old records there. And I discovered first, my first initiation into music really, except for what I told you about my mom and dad playing, was to hear the Borodin “Peasant Overture.” And that was a real charge to me. I couldn’t believe things could be like that musically. And I sat and must have listened to that thing for two hours. And then I started looking at some of the other things and there was a lot of Latin stuff there. And I listened to…
